_comment: DO NOT EDIT: Import this file in your Pterodactyl panel under Admin > Nests > Import Egg.
name: wolfXtg Telegram Bot
author: wolfXtg
description: Telegram automation bot with group management, media downloads, WhatsApp pairing, and more.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#  wolfXtg Bot — Pterodactyl Installation Script
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set -e

apt-get update -y -q
apt-get install -y -q curl git

cd /mnt/server

# ── 1. Clone or update the repository ─────────────
if [ -d .git ]; then
  echo "==> Updating existing installation..."
  git pull
else
  echo "==> Cloning repository..."
  git clone "${GIT_REPO}" .
fi

# ── 2. Install bot dependencies directly into bot/ ─
# We install inside bot/ rather than the workspace root
# to avoid the pnpm-only preinstall guard in package.json.
echo "==> Installing dependencies..."
cd bot
npm install --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund
cd ..

# ── 3. Create required data directory ──────────────
mkdir -p bot/data

# ── 4. Write .env — bot reads token from here ──────
echo "# wolfXtg Bot — auto-generated by Pterodactyl installer" > .env
echo "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}" >> .env

echo "==> Installation complete. Start the server to bring the bot online."

variables.name: Bot Token
variables.description: Your Telegram bot token from @BotFather. Saved to .env and loaded at every startup.

variables.name: Startup File
variables.description: Entry point for the bot. Do not change this.

variables.name: Git Repository
variables.description: The GitHub repository URL to clone during installation.
